name: Africa
alt: A world map with a large landmass highlighted, straddling the equator with hot desert across its northern half.
facts: Home to the Sahara, the largest hot desert in the world.
This is the only continent that sits on the equator and stretches into both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres equally.
It has more countries than any other continent — over 50 of them.

name: Antarctica
alt: A world map with the icy landmass at the very bottom of the globe highlighted.
facts: It's so cold that almost no people live here — but lots of penguins do!
This continent holds most of the world's fresh water, frozen into ice.
It has no permanent residents and no government of its own — scientists just visit to study it.

name: Asia
alt: A world map with the largest landmass highlighted, stretching from the middle of the globe to its eastern edge.
facts: This is the biggest continent — more than half of all the people in the world live here.
It's home to Mount Everest, the tallest mountain on Earth.
It stretches so far that sunrise on its eastern edge happens hours before sunrise on its western edge.

name: Australia
alt: A world map with one highlighted island-sized landmass, surrounded entirely by ocean, off by itself.
facts: This is the only continent that is also just one country.
It's home to animals found almost nowhere else, like kangaroos and koalas.
It's the flattest continent, with no big mountain ranges like the others have.

name: Europe
alt: A world map with a highlighted landmass made up of many small countries packed closely together.
facts: This continent packs more than 40 different countries close together.
It shares one giant landmass with Asia, though they're usually thought of as two different continents.
Many of its countries are small enough that you could drive across them in a single day.

name: North America
alt: A world map with a highlighted landmass spanning from icy northern land down to a narrow strip near the equator.
facts: This continent stretches all the way from icy Canada down to sunny Mexico.
It's home to the Great Lakes, which together hold about a fifth of the world's fresh surface water.
It has only three really big countries — Canada, the United States, and Mexico — plus many smaller ones in Central America and the Caribbean.

name: South America
alt: A world map with a highlighted, triangle-shaped landmass south of a narrow strip of land, crossed by the equator.
facts: Home to the Amazon rainforest, the largest rainforest on Earth.
It's home to the Andes, the longest mountain range in the world.
The Amazon River that runs through it carries more water than any other river on Earth.
